extraction.Name: Joseph Bissonette
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not desire his patent to his 480 acre allotment at the time it was issued; but he was advised by the Indian Agency that, if he did not accept it, that the allotment would finally be sold for taxes, as it would be assessed just the same, so he accepted the patent
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: in 1925, he sold the three quarters to Ed Hagel, of Pine Ridge, South Dakota, for $1850.00, Hagel paying all this in cash, excepting he traded deponent a saddle, valued at $85.00
extraction.Buyer: Ed Hagel, of Pine Ridge, South Dakota, for $1850.00 cash excepting a saddle valued at $85.00
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: kept up his taxes, but paid them under protest
extraction.Occupation/Income: he is a police for the United States Government, at Pine Ridge, South Dakota, this being his only source of income
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent, has good health; wife died in 1926; has two children to support, children have good health; considers $1850.00 was a very poor price for all this land; has never received any help from the County, State nor the United States Government; document sworn December 6, 1928
